The Eta Chapter of Delta Phi Epsilon is a co-ed foreign service society with a 97-year tradition of developing competent, creative, and ethical leaders for the world. Founded in 1929 to encourage fellowship, excellence, and professional development among those studying or engaged with international affairs and foreign service, the Eta Chapter continues to uphold this prestigious tradition.

DPE’s Eta Chapter actively seeks out the best and brightest students at The George Washington University. Regardless of major, students in good standing with the University who demonstrate exceptional academic and professional capability, an enthusiasm for international relations, a commitment to public service, and strong personal character are offered a place in our induction process. Alumni of Eta Chapter have gone on to become influential members of the American diplomatic corps, the defense community, international legal and business establishments, non-profits, and Congress. Fill out our interest form here.

name: 46th Patricia Roberts Harris Banquet
description:
The George Washington University Law School BLSA invites you to attend the 46th Annual Patricia Roberts Harris Awards Banquet.

The George Washington University Law School Black Law Students Association (BLSA) is pleased to announce the 46th Annual Patricia Roberts Harris Awards Banquet, which will be held on March 28th, 2026, at the JW Marriott in Washington, D.C. Mrs. Harris, a distinguished alumna of The George Washington University National Law Center (now The George Washington University Law School), achieved remarkable milestones in her career. After graduating at the top of her class in 1960, she became a dedicated public servant, earning numerous accolades and pioneering many firsts. Among her many achievements, she was the first African-American woman to serve as a United States Ambassador, a member of the United States Cabinet, and as Dean of an American law school (Howard University School of Law).


In the spirit of her incredible achievements, this banquet serves as an occasion to honor and recognize BLSA’s outstanding graduating students, alumni, and sponsors, as well as the law school’s dedicated faculty and staff. Building strong, enduring relationships with legal organizations across the District of Columbia is central to ensuring that students have opportunities to follow in Mrs. Harris’ path. Therefore, BLSA extends an invitation for you to join us in this celebration of our distinguished alumna and exceptional community.

Welcome to Fraternity and Sorority Life at GW! If you’ve recently joined a fraternity or sorority, the New Member Retreat is your next step—and it’s required.

You’ll explore the national and local history of these organizations, understand the values that continue to shape Greek Life today, and have honest conversations about hazing prevention and outdated traditions that no longer reflect who we are.

Led by the Office of Fraternity and Sorority Life, this retreat is also a chance to connect with new members from other chapters and councils, share your experiences, and start building a more inclusive, supportive community.

Check-in begins at 9:30 AM, and you must attend the full event to receive credit—so mark your calendar, bring your energy, and get ready to grow.

name: CAPS Workshops: Resilient Minds Series Fall 2025
description:
Join the Resilient Minds Series, workshops and events hosted by CAPS, where you'll gain practical tips to support your mental health, build resilience, and connect with others in the GW community.

These workshops are designed to help you develop coping strategies, manage stress, and enhance your overall well-being. Whether you're navigating academic challenges or personal struggles, the Resilient Minds Series offers a supportive space to learn, grow, and thrive. All students are welcome to participate! Students are free to attend as many or as few sessions as needed. Interested students can register and learn more by completing this form or contacting CAPS at capsoutreach@gwu.edu.

name: IM 6v6 Indoor Volleyball
description:
Sport: 6v6 Indoor Volleyball
Location: Lerner Health & Wellness Center, 4th Floor
Timeframe: Registration: 10/13-10/22, Season: 10/26-12/5
Format: 3 week regular season + 1 week single-elimination playoff bracket

Overview:
The 6v6 Indoor Volleyball Intramural League offers a fun, inclusive, and competitive environment for players of all skill levels. Teams will compete weekly in a round-robin format leading into a playoff bracket to determine the league champion. Games are held on Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday evenings.
